title: Prediction
prompt: What is the main job of client-side routing in a React app?

options.label: It asks the server for a new HTML document for every navigation.
It replaces local component state for all UI changes.
It maps browser URLs to React screens without a full document reload.

responses.server-renders-every-page: Not quite. That describes traditional full document navigation. Client-side routing keeps the app running and changes the rendered route.
responses.url-to-screen: Correct. Client-side routing connects URLs to React-rendered screens while preserving app runtime.
responses.replaces-state: Not quite. Routing identifies screens. Local state still handles interaction inside a screen.

metadata.reason: Catches the misconception that routing is either server-only or a replacement for state.
